summary: SSO tenant-alias claim collision prevents cross-project tool access for internal CI runner
description:
Issue summary: Several internal CI jobs and cross-project debug tooling began failing to authenticate after a tenant-migration change. Impact: Multiple oncall and engineering workflows blocked — builds can’t fetch secrets and dashboards return 403. Scope appears limited to services that rely on the tenant-alias claim emitted by the identity proxy during SSO token exchange.

Observed start: 2026-02-28 15:20 UTC.

Context: We rolled out a tenant alias normalization change in the identity-proxy last week to support new org aliasing. Post-rollout, some tokens include the new alias in the "tenant_alias" claim while others still present the legacy alias, and downstream tooling performs strict equality when resolving permission namespaces. This has led to claim collisions where two different alias values map to a single internal project namespace, causing RBAC resolution to fail with 403s.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Authenticate via Okta to the internal CI runner service (ci-runner).
2) Capture the ID token / access token after exchange.
3) Inspect the tenant_alias claim payload.
4) Attempt to access /v1/secrets or start a pipeline using that token.
5) Observe 403 for tokens where tenant_alias != expected exact alias stored in permission index.
observed_behavior: Affected tokens show either 'rdw:team-alpha' or 'rdw-team-alpha' in tenant_alias claim depending on which identity-proxy replica handled the exchange. Authorization service expects a canonical 'rdw-team-alpha' and rejects the alternate form. Result: CI jobs receive 403 during secret fetch, runbook access denied for debugging, and some internal dashboards show permission errors.
expected_behavior: Identity tokens should contain a stable, canonical tenant_alias value or the authorization service must accept normalized variants so RBAC lookup succeeds regardless of minor alias formatting differences.

comments: 2026-02-28 16:05 - Aisha Khan (Support): Initial triage — confirmed multiple CI pipelines failed at the same time. Gathered tokens from affected runners and attached to ticket. Notified SRE channel #infra-auth.

2026-02-28 17:12 - Ethan Li (SRE): Reproduced locally by hitting staging identity-proxy. Found inconsistent tenant_alias formatting across replicas. Suspect feature-flagged normalization rollout partially enabled; rolling back flag on two replicas to see effect.

2026-02-28 18:03 - Maya Patel (Reporter): Confirmed that after rollback some pipelines resumed. Providing list of affected pipeline IDs and two failing job logs in the ticket attachments (linked in Confluence).

2026-03-01 09:40 - Ethan Li (SRE): Implemented temporary normalization middleware in authz service to accept both 'rdw:team-alpha' and 'rdw-team-alpha' forms. Patch deployed to prod-authz-canary. Immediate effect: previously failing pipelines moved to queued state. Need permanent fix in identity-proxy or a canonicalization layer upstream.

2026-03-02 11:22 - Priya Nair (Identity): Confirmed rollout of tenant-alias normalization flag was staged but the canary protocol did not include legacy alias backward-compatibility. Preparing a PR to add deterministic canonicalization at token issuance and update docs.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Partial rollout of alias normalization in identity-proxy caused heterogeneous token formats. Evidence: mixed tenant_alias values in proxy logs and rollout timeline aligned with incident start.
Hypothesis 2: Authorization service performs strict string match against permission index. Evidence: authz logs show NOT_FOUND for alternate alias forms.
Interim mitigation: added normalization layer to authz to map variant forms to canonical namespace.
Root cause: lack of canonicalization and a missing compatibility guard in identity-proxy PR. A coordinated migration plan was not followed — no smoke test that exercised cross-replica token issuance.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: normalization fallback added to authorization service (hotfix) and deployed to prod - reduced impact to near zero. Permanent fix: identity-proxy PR #594 merged which canonicalizes tenant_alias at issuance and adds a feature-flag guard. Deployment notes: rolled out canary with traffic shaping over 6 hours, validated token formats via smoke tests.
Follow-ups: INT-213105 created to add end-to-end smoke test for tenant alias variants, and a runbook update to include alias-migration checklist.
Status: Monitoring, awaiting final validation window before closing.
